ai.description: This small shrub frog measures 20–25 mm. It has a brownish-grey dorsum with irregular dark markings and a distinct white throat. Diagnostic features include a pointed snout and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes sanjappai* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or golden-yellow iris, which contrasts sharply with the darker, mottled brown body coloration.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes sanjappai inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, specifically residing in the canopy of shola grasslands above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes sanjappai is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes sanjappai* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes sanjappai* is endemic to the high-altitude shola grasslands and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes sanjappai* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
